commit.message:
feat(operations): rotary heights read as radii about the fitted axis

A rotary operation can now read a height as a radius about the fitted
rotation axis, not only as a world-Z plane. The stored form is
`RadialHeight { source, offset }`: the source is the stock OD, the
model max radius, or an absolute radius. The fields are optional -
`clearance_r`, `retract_r`, `top_r`, `bottom_r` on Rotary Contour and
Rotary Parallel, and `clearance_r` + `top_r` on Rotary Offset. `None`
keeps the Z-plane law byte-for-byte; the `*_z` fields stay.

One resolver (`app::operation::radial_heights`) fits the same axis the
generators pose about. The radial gate refuses, at Create, Edit and
ChangeKind, a clearance or retract radius that stands inside the work,
or a cut band that crosses (top below bottom). Refusals name the field
and the radius. The Heights tab draws one check row per slot with a
From combo and an echo of the resolved radius; each row scopes its
field ids with `push_id`, so two enabled slots never collapse into one
egui id. The viewport rings are additive to the Z-plane rectangles.
New contour and parallel ops seed the clearance and retract radii at
the stock OD + 5 / + 10; the band radii stay None. PROJECT_VERSION 74:
the migration is a comment-only no-op, the new fields are serde
defaults, and an old project reads all radii None.

Pinned by: the motion `rotary` radial law tests, the app
`rotary_verify` suite (refusals by name, stored-height edits, v74
round-trip), the ui `radial_rows_tests` (rows, combos, echoes,
per-slot scoping) and the radial-axis cache test in
`height_memo_tests`.

Decisions: docs/decisions/2774-rotary-heights.md

Fixes #2774

feat(multiaxis): window the rotary cut band by radii about the axis

fitted axis, not two Z planes. Rotary Contour keeps whole rings by tip
radius (band_select); Rotary Parallel trims each skin-following pass at
the band edges (band_trim); Rotary Offset floors its develop ladder at
the bottom radius. A band that crosses no part skin refuses by name at
the generate, with both radii and the reach printed. The command gate
also refuses a top radius at or above the clearance cylinder, so no cut
rides where the rapids travel. All-None stays the Z-plane law, byte for
byte. The band helpers live in multiaxis/radial_band.rs.

Pinned by band tests in crates/motion/tests/rotary.rs and command-level
tests in crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs.

Fixes #2774

fix(multiaxis): a wrapping parallel band hands the base path on unchanged

#2774 pin: a band whose cylinders cover the path's whole radial reach
trims nothing, but the per-span solve still chopped runs where the retip
read dips past the axis, and the relink turned each chop into a retract,
index and plunge. band_trim now reads the clamped reach first and returns
the base path unchanged when every chord stands in the band.

Fixes #2774

feat(multiaxis): the radial heights and the cut band land on the
current ladder

The held #2774 feature (rotary heights read as radii about the fitted
axis, the band windowing, the wrapping band's hand-off), cherry-picked
from FlamingFireCoding:issue/2774-rotary-heights onto the current main,
and completed the way main has moved since:

- The project ladder steps v84 -> v85 (#2774): the rotary kinds may
  state `clearance_r`, `retract_r`, `top_r`, `bottom_r`; absent is the
  Z-plane law every v84 file ran, so a v84 file steps up unchanged. A
  v84 reader refuses a v85 file rather than drop the stated radii.
  The rung's comment sits in apply.rs's ladder and file.rs's doc, and
  the params DTO's own doc comments name v85.
- The stated-axis entries (#2772) take the radial heights: the
  generate calls `rotary_contour_stated`/`rotary_parallel_over_stated`/
  `rotary_offset_stated` with the resolved radii, and the plain entries
  keep the fit inside them.
- The heights-page rows and the radial rows coexist: the rotary page
  keeps main's editor shape and adds the band's four rows on the
  Heights tab; the heights memo keeps main's unresolved note beside
  the radial memo.
- The digest's pocket-door arms (RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough,
  AdvancedSwarf) move to `params/multiaxis_pocket.rs` and the radial
  height writer to `params/digest.rs` - the 400-line law.
- New-op call sites of the rotated enums on main (first traverse,
  rotary traverse, the tests) state the four radii None, so every
  Z-plane op reads byte for byte as before.

Pinned by the motion rotary suite, the app rotary suites
(`rotary_verify` incl. the v85 round trip and the band refusals), the
project-version suites, the ui lib suite and clippy -D warnings.

Refs #2774

fix(multiaxis): the band trim keeps every kept span's corner, so the
retip read and the envelope law agree on slanted skins

#3490: the banded Rotary Parallel verified with a false gouge -
`Envelope { at: 38, gouge_mm: 1.544, rest_mm: 0.096 }` on a radial
band 4.0..5.5 over the r6/r5 stepped bar - and the post refused a
legal program.

The diagnosis, read against the verifier's real-envelope law
(`stock_sim::facet_gouge`, the exact distance of each model triangle
to each reconstructed ball center, never weakened here): the trim's
kept-stretch join GLUED touching spans by extending the previous
output move's end - two arc-fit chords of a run became one straight
chord. On the raster's wrap chains (the arc around the cone's edge,
its ball centers riding the radius-8.5 ring) the glued chord dips
1.46 mm below the arc the base plan rode, and the ball there stands
1.4554 mm from the cone facet - the 1.5446 mm gouge the envelope law
reported, move for move. The retip read itself
(`hypot(y, z + r) - r`, the ball-center radius minus the ball) is
exact where the pose is the radial: every cut move's emitted tip
rides it. What lied was the kept geometry the glue made.

The fix: touching spans stay consecutive Feed records. The relink
below already reads consecutive non-lift Feeds as one run, so the
spans keep one cut - never a link between them - and the run's
polyline survives with every corner. The wrapping-band early-out
keeps its behaviour, and the correct refusals stand: a band that
crosses no part skin still refuses by name at the generate
(`a_band_that_crosses_no_skin_is_refused_by_name`,
`a_parallel_band_that_crosses_no_skin_is_refused_by_name`), and a
gouging path still blocks the post - the envelope law is untouched.

Pinned by `rotary_verify::the_stated_radial_heights_move_the_generated_path`
(red at the held branch's commit with the reported verdict, green
here on the untouched envelope law), the motion band tests
(`the_parallel_band_cuts_between_two_cylinders`,
`a_band_that_wraps_the_whole_skin_adds_no_links`), and the full
motion, sim, app and ui lib suites.

Fixes #3490

fix(multiaxis): the stated tip radii convert to the links, and the band keeps its closed one-sided edges

The #4379 review rework, the motion side (findings 1-3 of nine):

- The contour's radial relink treated the stated radii as the planning
  centers' radii, so `posed` backed every emitted point off one ball
  radius along its pose and a stated clearance R6 with a 2 mm ball
  exited at R5 - the reviewer's probe read a 2.5 mm gouge into the
  r6 wall at app level and the post refused a legal program. The relink
  now takes the ball radius and applies ONE tip-to-center conversion to
  every contour link (the opening plunge, every retract, index and
  re-entry: the ball center stands one ball radius OUTSIDE the stated
  radius), the same law rotary_links::radial_relink already applies to
  the parallel twin, so the posed tip stands AT the stated radius on
  every link and every rapid.
- A Bottom radius with no Top returned None and the generator silently
  dropped the stated floor (Bottom R1.5 produced the unband moves).
  band_window now honors each supported one-sided band: Bottom-only
  runs from the floor cylinder out to the skin's end, Top-only from the
  axis out to the stated ceiling, for all three rotary kinds.
- A span ON a band cylinder was dropped when another span forced the
  trim (the review's probe: a constant-radius span on the bottom
  cylinder lost its end). each_band_span keeps constant and tangent
  spans with one closed-interval rule, so both exact edges stand,
  including mixed paths that enter and leave the band.

Pinned by `the_stated_radii_are_the_tips_radii_on_every_link`,
`the_stated_contour_radii_clear_the_work` (the reviewer's app probe:
stated R8/R6.5 on the d12.4 bar verifies silent, the exit at R8 - it
read `Envelope { gouge_mm: 2.5 }` before), the one-sided band tests,
and the closed-edge law in `radial_band_tests.rs`.

Refs #3490

fix(operation): the radial resolver reads the judged axis, and every set radius is validated before it is stored

The #4379 review rework, the app side (findings 4-5 of nine):

- The resolver always free-fitted the axis while generation can turn
  about a STATED one - on the R5 sphere fixture the generator judges the
  stated Z axis while resolve_radial rejected the same source with
  "every axis fits this model equally". radial_context now takes the
  axis through the same law generate runs (rotary_stated::axis_lines,
  judged against the source's faces; the free fit only when nothing is
  stated), so the gate, the panel echo and the viewport ring answer for
  the line the toolpath really rides.
- The gate discarded resolution errors (a stock radius with no stock
  passed silently), is_sane omitted the radial fields, and
  CreateOperation::new accepted both a NaN clearance and an absolute
  Bottom radius of -1. Every set radial field is now validated before
  storage: RadialHeight::is_sane keeps a finite offset and an absolute
  radius never under the axis, is_sane checks each set field on the
  twins and the wrap ladder, and radial_gate surfaces the resolution
  failure, refuses a resolved radius under the axis, and keeps the
  ordering and band-under-rapids laws. The same door runs on create,
  edit, paste and retype.

Pinned by a_stated_axis_resolves_the_radii_generation_judges,
a_radial_radius_that_is_no_radius_is_refused_at_the_command and
a_radial_radius_its_source_cannot_answer_is_refused_by_name.

Refs #3490

fix(ui): the radial rings stand on an orthonormal basis, and a valid zero radius echoes as one

The #4379 review rework, the display side (findings 6-7 of nine, and the
display half of finding 4):

- The viewport ring's second perpendicular was computed by passing
  `dir x u` back through `off_axis`, which picks another helper and
  turns that direction into one the ring's plane does not contain: an
  X axis collapsed its ring to a line through sqrt(2) x the stated
  radius, a Z axis laid the second vector along the axis itself. The
  basis is now orthonormal (`u` off the axis, `v` the unit `dir x u`),
  and every generated ring point stands in the plane square to the
  judged axis at the stated radius - pinned for X, Y, Z and an oblique
  axis, and end to end through the overlay for the open operation.
- The rings read the same judged axis the generators turn about: the
  memo's key now carries the axis statement, the machine's work-turning
  rotary lines and the work offset origin, so a new statement refits
  the ring once and a still frame keeps it.
- Bottom R0 is valid and is the checkbox default, but the echo reported
  "unresolved: the radius is not positive". The echo displays the
  resolved zero for the field that permits it, and the page test
  drives the check row the way a user's click lands.

Pinned by the radial_view_tests basis and plane pins,
the_overlay_rings_stand_in_planes_about_the_judged_axis,
the_radial_axis_cache_follows_a_new_axis_statement and
the_default_bottom_radius_echoes_its_valid_zero.

Refs #3490

chore(examples): the continuous 4-axis example steps to the current v85 writer

The writer advanced to v85 (the radial heights rung of #2774) but the
committed example stayed a v84 file with its old stamp, so three
continuous_4axis_part tests failed that pass on bare main. The example
project is regenerated by the suite's own WRITE_GOLDEN path: the diff is
the version number and the operation stamp - no stored parameter, setup,
machine or program statement moved, and the committed .nc posts
unchanged from the refreshed project (the post test reads it back
move for move).

Goldens moved:
- examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj: version 84 -> 85 and the
  operation stamp refresh. Nothing else in the file changed.
- examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc: unchanged.

This step is a compatibility break, as the ladder's own comment states:
every file this build writes says v85, and a v84 reader refuses it
rather than drop the stated radii and post a clearance shape that does
not match the stored radii.

BREAKING CHANGE: project files written by this build say v85; a v84
reader refuses them. A v84 file steps up to v85 unchanged (the radial
fields are serde-defaulted to the Z-plane law it wrote).

Refs #3490
